frameworks.name: Rule of One
frameworks.definition: Launch with one product, one social channel, one marketing channel, and one sales channel; when revenue plateaus, add exactly one increment to exactly one of those categories before expanding further.

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition) argues that simplicity scales and diversification is a distraction: when launching a new business, start with one product, one social media channel, one marketing channel, and one sales channel. Spreading across multiple categories before mastering one prevents the expertise accumulation needed to break through early revenue plateaus.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: early-stage consumer product or DTC business
pre-plateau phase (before first revenue ceiling is hit)
claims.mechanism: Concentrating on one unit per category forces the founder to become an expert in that single channel before adding complexity, whereas simultaneous multi-channel launches split attention and prevent mastery of any single channel.
bounded_by: Does not prescribe remaining at one forever — expansion is appropriate once a plateau is reached

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition) holds that the correct response to a revenue plateau is to add exactly one increment to exactly one growth category (product line, social channel, marketing channel, sales channel, or demographic) rather than expanding across multiple categories simultaneously. Each plateau break adds one more unit to one category.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: triggered only after a revenue plateau is reached on the current category configuration
claims.mechanism: Adding one increment at a time lets the business develop expertise in the new category while keeping operational complexity manageable; multi-category expansion at once compounds the learning curve and increases failure risk.
bounded_by: The rule applies per plateau; it does not prevent reaching a state with multiple products and multiple channels over time

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition) describes a sequential plateau-break path for DTC brands targeting revenue stages from $10,000 to $100,000 to $1,000,000 per month, in which each stage requires identifying which single category (product, channel, demographic, or sales platform) is the binding constraint and adding exactly one new unit in that category.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia

numbers.axis: monthly revenue plateau thresholds for DTC brand (Bloom Nutrition framework)

bounded_by: Greg LaVecchia acknowledges this is specific to how Bloom Nutrition broke through revenue ceilings; generalizability to non-DTC businesses is not asserted

examples.text: When Bloom Nutrition launched, Greg LaVecchia applied the Rule of One strictly: one product (a pre-workout formula for women who lift weights and are sensitive to caffeine), one social media channel (Instagram), one marketing channel (Instagram), and one sales channel (Shopify). When the pre-workout revenue plateaued, the team debated which single category to expand: add a second product (e.g., a high-energy pre-workout for women not sensitive to caffeine, which became Bloom Pre-Workout High Energy), add a second sales channel (Amazon), add a second marketing channel (Google, YouTube, or billboards), or target a new demographic. They chose one of those options rather than expanding on all fronts simultaneously.

practices.text: When hitting a revenue plateau, before adding any new channel or product, explicitly identify which single category (product, social channel, marketing channel, sales channel, or demographic) is most likely the binding constraint, then add only one increment to that category.
